name: Torsade-de-pointes Syndrome with Short Coupling Interval
aliases: Idiopathic Ventricular Fibrillation with Short Coupling Interval

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Short Coupling Interval Torsade-de-Pointes Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Presence of ventricular premature beats with a short coupling interval (<300 ms) initiating torsade-de-pointes
Normal QT interval on baseline electrocardiogram
No evidence of structural heart disease on imaging studies
Documented episodes of torsade-de-pointes ventricular tachycardia on ECG or Holter monitoring
Family history of sudden cardiac death or ventricular arrhythmias

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All major criteria including documented torsade-de-pointes with short coupling interval, normal QT interval, and absence of structural heart disease must be met.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other causes of torsade-de-pointes such as long QT syndrome and electrolyte abnormalities.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Polymorphic ventricular tachycardia with short coupling interval
searchTerms: fast abnormal heartbeats with short gap

pathognomonic.symptomName: Syncope due to transient ventricular arrhythmia
pathognomonic.notes: Transient loss of consciousness related to arrhythmia
searchTerms: passing out due to irregular heartbeat
temporary heart rhythm loss causing fainting

common.symptomName: Palpitations associated with premature ventricular contractions
common.notes: Patient may report awareness of irregular heartbeat
Potentially fatal arrhythmia requiring emergency intervention

common.symptomName: Ventricular premature beats with short coupling interval
common.notes: Detected on ECG or Holter monitoring

common.symptomName: Normal baseline QT interval on ECG
searchTerms: standard QT interval on heart test

occasional.notes: Arrhythmias may be triggered by physical exertion

occasional.symptomName: Mild chest discomfort during arrhythmia episodes
searchTerms: slight chest discomfort with irregular heartbeat
chest unease during heart rhythm issues

rare.symptomName: Seizure-like activity secondary to cerebral hypoperfusion
rare.notes: Due to transient cerebral ischemia during arrhythmia
searchTerms: seizure-like episodes from low brain blood flow
mild heart muscle weakness after arrest

imaging: Normal echocardiogram with no structural heart disease
Normal cardiac MRI excluding fibrosis or cardiomyopathy
genetic: Possible mutations in genes related to cardiac ion channels (e.g., RyR2, CALM1) though often idiopathic
other: ECG showing normal QT interval with frequent premature ventricular contractions having short coupling intervals

distinguishingFeatures: Genetic mutations in KCNQ1, KCNH2, SCN5A
Characteristic ECG pattern with ST elevation in V1-V3
Risk of ventricular fibrillation without QT prolongation

redFlags: Sudden cardiac arrest or unexplained sudden death in young individuals
Ventricular arrhythmias refractory to standard antiarrhythmic therapy
references: Priori SG, et al. Short-coupled variant of torsade de pointes: clinical features and therapeutic options. Circulation. 2005.
